scenes.title: Sign in once, the CLI keeps the token

cues.text: The Symphony plugin brings Symphony into Tern.
It shows what the agents do, opens live chats, and covers the merger and team administration.
Run Symphony: Sign in, then enter your team's address and the API token an admin created for you.
The token is masked. The symphony CLI stores it in the system keychain.
cues.say: The token is masked. The symphony C L I stores it in the system keychain.

cues.text: Tern never stores it. The plugin asks the CLI for the token and keeps it in memory only.
cues.say: Tern never stores it. The plugin asks the C L I for the token and keeps it in memory only.

cues.text: Install in Tern adds the live chat agent, the MCP server for your omp, and this panel.
cues.say: Install in Tern adds the live chat agent, the M C P server for your omp, and this panel.

cues.text: When you are not signed in, the panel and the status line show the next step.
If Symphony goes down, the panel keeps the last data and shows Offline.

scenes.title: Needs input, actions and the status line

cues.text: Control Alt S opens the Dashboard.
It shows the day's numbers, and the providers' rate limits of the last hour.
Sessions that need input come first, with the agent's question and its options.
Press A to answer. Pick an option, or write your own answer.
Press M to send a message. If the agent is running, the message joins the current turn.
Press I to interrupt, after a confirmation.
Press T to take over. Symphony takeover then runs in a new tab.
The status line shows how many agents run, and how many need input.
It is highlighted when an agent waits for you, and says paused or offline.

scenes.title: Steer, follow up, interrupt, take over

cues.text: Sessions lists every session. The bracket keys filter Active, Needs input, Ended or All.
Control Alt A picks a session and opens its live chat in a new tab.
It is a native Tern chat through symphony acp, with the history and the live events.
cues.say: It is a native Tern chat through symphony A C P, with the history and the live events.

cues.text: While the agent runs, your message steers the current turn.
When it is idle, the message is a follow-up. When it asks, the message is the answer.
To stop the agent, type slash interrupt.
Take over holds the ticket, downloads the conversation and the branch, and opens omp on your machine.
Return it with symphony release.
Tickets shows each ticket's state in Symphony and on the board, the attempt, the cost and the pull request.
Symphony does not dispatch a ticket that a person holds.
Return to Symphony releases it, and the agents can work on it again.
Each repository has its own merger. Control Alt M opens the Merger view.
Mergers lists them: whether each one runs, who holds its train lease, and its current batch.
Each table has a Repository column, so pull requests of two repositories never mix.
On the selected pull request, B bypasses the review. It asks for a reason for the audit log.
Q requeues the pull request, and L releases it.
Each action goes to the merger of that pull request's repository.
Five views are read-only, for every role.
Repositories lists where Symphony dispatches tickets.
Infrastructure shows the services and the cluster resources.
Telemetry shows usage by model, by month and by session.
Learnings shows the retrospectives and learning pull requests.
Audit lists what people and agents asked Symphony to do.
When a source is stale or unavailable, the view says which one.

scenes.title: Models per role and provider keys

cues.text: The Admin view needs an admin token.
Models sets the model and the thinking level of each role.
Enter picks a model from the pinned omp catalog, then the thinking level.
The change stays marked until you publish it with P and a reason.
If someone else published first, nothing is overwritten.
The rollout shows which consumers already applied the new generation.
Providers stores the API keys that the models use.
C sets or replaces a key in a hidden field. The key is write-only: it never comes back through the API.
It applies on each agent's next attempt, without a restart.

scenes.title: Tokens, MCP servers and team omp

cues.text: Tokens creates team API tokens, each with a name, a role and an expiry.
A viewer watches, an operator also acts, and an admin administers.
A new token appears only once. After I saved it, it is gone.
X revokes a token at once, after a confirmation.
MCP servers give agents more tools. Each role gets only the servers enabled for it.
cues.say: M C P servers give agents more tools. Each role gets only the servers enabled for it.

cues.text: Enter tests a server and lists its tools.
Secret headers are write-only. The gateway adds them, so no secret reaches an agent.
Team omp shows the workers' omp defaults. S applies them to your omp, in a separate profile.
The palette has a command for each view.
Control Alt S opens the Dashboard, Control Alt M the Merger, and Control Alt A a live chat.
In the panel, tab switches views, the arrows or J and K select, and enter opens the chat.
R refreshes, and Control P pauses or resumes the daemon.
Each footer shows only the keys that your role can use.
A confirmation opens above the footer. Enter confirms, and escape cancels.
Pause, bypass and publish need a reason of at least eight characters, for the audit log.
